name: Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme
description:
PMEGP helps eligible applicants establish new micro enterprises in non-farm activities through bank finance and margin-money subsidy. The business still needs a viable project, the required own contribution and a lender willing to sanction the loan.

Margin money is a back-ended subsidy linked to the financed project. It should not be treated as unrestricted cash available to spend before the enterprise is established.
eligibility:
The normal new-unit route does not cover an existing business simply seeking reimbursement for earlier expenditure. Earlier government subsidy, the applicant’s eligibility, education requirements for specified project sizes and the scheme’s activity exclusions must be examined before filing.

Describe what the enterprise will manufacture or deliver, which machines and premises it needs, and how it will earn enough to meet operating expenses and loan repayment. A generic project report with an inflated machinery schedule weakens the lending case as well as the subsidy application.
benefits:
The maximum project cost eligible for subsidy is ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for the service or business sector. The applicable subsidy depends on the beneficiary category and whether the location is rural or urban. The published framework provides higher assistance for qualifying special categories.

The lender may consider finance beyond the subsidy-linked ceiling in permitted circumstances, but that does not extend subsidy to the additional amount. Capital expenditure and working capital also have separate constraints within the project cost.
application_process:
Assemble identity and category evidence where applicable, the project location, education records where required, quotations, premises arrangements and the funding plan. Separate the proposed assets from working capital and excluded items. The sales and expense assumptions should be explainable from the activity and intended market.

The application proceeds through the official PMEGP process and the relevant implementing agency and bank. Bank appraisal, training or other prescribed steps, implementation and verification are part of the route. A portal submission is not a sanction, and a loan sanction should not be confused with final subsidy adjustment.

For an existing PMEGP loan, retain the sanction, disbursement, margin-money and verification records before assessing any pending adjustment. The exact stage is more useful than a statement that subsidy has “not arrived”.

Read the revised PMEGP guidelines and the Government’s May 2026 PMEGP explanation. Confirm the current application process and applicable financial-year instructions with the implementing agency before committing to a submission schedule.

name: Haryana Gramin Udyogik Vikas Yojna (HGUVY)
description:
HGUVY was Haryana’s HEEP 2020 package for new micro enterprises in rural areas of B, C and D category blocks. It combined capital support, term-loan interest assistance and generator-set assistance. Its rural-location test was specific: the site had to fall under the sole jurisdiction of a village panchayat.

A village name in the postal address is not sufficient evidence of that status. The relevant revenue estate, land records and panchayat jurisdiction must match the enterprise’s actual site.
eligibility: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.
benefits:
The July 2021 notification provided capital assistance on qualifying plant, machinery and building investment, separate interest support on term borrowing and a generator-set component. Its capital rate was 15%, with different ceilings for general-category and women or SC entrepreneurs. Each component had its own cost and timing basis.

The definition of a new enterprise linked qualifying investment, commercial production or term-loan sanction to the notified period. The unit had to remain in production, and the notification imposed continuing conditions for the assisted investment and generator set.

A particularly important restriction concerned PMEGP: a unit that had received PMEGP subsidy was not entitled to HGUVY benefits other than the specified generator-set component. Do not add the headline benefits from both programmes into one funding plan.

name: Generator Set Subsidy Scheme in Haryana
description:
Haryana’s Generator Set Subsidy Scheme was notified for small and medium enterprises in rural C and D category blocks under HEEP 2020. It addressed the cost of a generator for continuity of power. It was a separate programme from PMEGP.

The official definition was not restricted to diesel: it described generator sets using diesel, CNG, petrol or other fuels. The machine’s fuel, capacity and operating permissions must therefore be considered alongside its scheme treatment.
eligibility: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.
benefits:
The June 2021 notification used a per-kVA amount subject to a percentage of the generator cost, with different percentage limits for small and medium enterprises. That structure means the capacity figure and the purchase price both matter. A larger set does not create an unlimited claim.

The unit had to be in a rural area under village-panchayat jurisdiction and in regular production. The generator had to be bought from an authorised dealer or manufacturer within the applicable period and remain intact and operational for five years. The scheme provided for inspections.

Micro enterprises had a separate generator component within HGUVY. Selecting the enterprise classification is therefore necessary before choosing the notification.

name: Testing Equipment Assistance in Haryana
description:
Haryana’s 2021 Testing Equipment Assistance Scheme supported equipment used to check raw materials or finished products. For a manufacturer, the practical value is stronger control over product quality through an in-house testing capability. The equipment’s testing function matters more than a supplier describing it as a “quality machine”.

The Haryana Testing Equipment Assistance Scheme notified on 8 June 2021 provided support for qualifying MSMEs. It should be distinguished from reimbursement of an external laboratory’s test charges and from assistance for obtaining a quality certificate.
eligibility: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.
benefits:
The 2021 scheme provided 50% support for the purchase of testing equipment, subject to a maximum of ₹20 lakh per year. It excluded second-hand testing equipment. The unit had to be in commercial production, meet the scheme’s registration and other eligibility conditions, and remain in regular production at disbursement.

The purchased equipment was to be retained for five years without disposal unless the competent authority approved it. This makes the asset register and continuing physical availability important after the initial claim, not just at purchase.
application_process:
The notified route was an online application to the Directorate of MSME, followed by District MSME Centre scrutiny and inspection. The inspection connects the documents to the actual equipment at the unit. Clarifications should answer the particular technical or cost issue raised, with consistent invoices and records.

Does a production machine qualify because it improves quality?

Improving quality is not enough by itself. The application needs to establish that the proposed asset is testing equipment within the applicable scheme.

Is a quality certificate part of the same claim?

A certificate and a testing asset are different expenditure heads. See Quality Certification Assistance for the separate topic and assess any overlap in funding before claiming.

name: Electricity Duty Exemption in Haryana
description:
Under Haryana’s HEEP 2020 notification, electricity duty exemption reduced or removed the electricity-duty component for an eligible enterprise. It does not mean free electricity, and it does not by itself remove energy charges, demand charges or other items on a power bill.

Haryana’s June 2021 HEEP notification provided different exemption periods for enterprise and sector categories. The practical starting point is to identify the applicable category, the site’s block and the date from which the exemption could run.
eligibility: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.
benefits:
The notification distinguished MSMEs, large and mega projects, thrust sectors, specified services and other categories. For example, ordinary manufacturing MSMEs had a different period from the listed service enterprises. A firm’s size or Udyam registration alone did not establish which line of the notification applied.

An exemption also needs the correct electricity connection. The meter, consumer account, enterprise name and industrial site should align with the application. If an expansion uses an existing connection, establish what investment and consumption the approval actually covers.
application_process:
Collect the electricity bill and connection details, commercial-production evidence, applicable registration records, block identification and relevant project approvals. Bills should show the duty charged separately so that the claimed treatment can be checked. Preserve any earlier exemption order and the period it specifies.

For a running unit, reconcile the order with subsequent bills and raise a supported query where the treatment differs. For a new project, first establish which current notification applies and the authority’s application requirements. Do not assume an old approval for another unit transfers with a property or power connection.

Is electricity duty the same as the power tariff?

No. Tariff and duty are distinct bill components. A tariff assistance scheme and duty exemption must be assessed and recorded separately.

Does every B, C or D block project get the same benefit?

No. The historic notification also used enterprise and sector categories. The applicable classification and dates must be proved.

name: Fire Equipment and Safety Compliance Assistance
description:
A fire-equipment subsidy enquiry should begin with the safety work being carried out and the scheme that covers it. Haryana’s 8 June 2021 Safety Compliance Scheme supported safety audits and qualifying capital equipment or expenditure for safety measures. The official title is broader than “Fire Equipment Subsidy”.

Buying an extinguisher, installing a fire system and completing a safety audit are different actions. A scheme claim needs to explain the expenditure and how it meets the applicable notification. It also needs to remain separate from obtaining a fire approval or maintaining required safety arrangements.
eligibility: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.
benefits:
Under the 2021 notification, safety-audit reimbursement was 75% of eligible expense, capped at ₹1 lakh. Assistance for qualifying safety capital equipment and expenditure was 50%, subject to different caps for A, B, C and D blocks, once in five years. The capital ceiling therefore cannot be stated correctly without the unit’s block category.

The notification linked the safety-audit benefit to implementation of the audit recommendations. It specified an audit by auditors of an ISO-certified agency, new safety investment and an operating MSME that met the registration and applicable approval conditions. An audit report left without action did not meet the stated basis for audit assistance.
application_process:
The useful starting point is the audit report and its recommendations. Link each claimed item to the safety issue it addresses, then show the approved specification, invoice, payment and installation. Record which recommendations have been completed and which remain outstanding.

For a fire-safety system, equipment descriptions should identify the actual installation, not only a bundled supplier amount. Civil work, equipment and professional services may need separate treatment. The safety professional’s design and implementation records provide context for the claim; government incentive approval does not certify that the facility is safe.

The original notification required a complete claim within three months of the relevant audit or equipment event, or notification, whichever was later. Project chronology and any earlier submission therefore matter. District scrutiny and site inspection form part of the notified process.

name: Stamp Duty Reimbursement in Haryana
description:
Haryana’s HEEP 2020 stamp-duty reimbursement concerned duty paid on a qualifying land transaction for the enterprise. Its value depends on the applicable policy and the actual stamp duty paid, not on the entire purchase price of the property.

The June 2021 Haryana Stamp Duty Refund Scheme under HEEP 2020 differentiated block and enterprise categories and linked several benefits to commencement of commercial production within five years of the land purchase. Buying industrial land did not complete the claim conditions on its own.
eligibility: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.
benefits:
For a claim, the sale deed, stamp-duty payment and land particulars need to connect to the enterprise and the project for which support is sought. Check the purchaser’s legal identity, the property’s permitted use and the date the qualifying business began production.

The original notification provided different percentages for categories including general MSMEs, thrust sectors and other specified enterprises. A rate quoted for one category should not be used for a different business. Lease-related or sector-policy assistance also needs its own source rather than being inferred from a land-purchase provision.

name: CGTMSE Fee Reimbursement in Haryana
description:
CGTMSE fees are not automatically refundable when a business repays its loan. The Haryana scheme commonly described as the “CGTMSE fee refund” is a state reimbursement provision, officially notified as the Collateral Free Credit Guarantee Scheme under HEEP 2020. It concerned eligible micro enterprises in Haryana and the guarantee-cover fee charged by their financial institution or bank.

That distinction answers the first practical question: a state incentive claim, a bank’s correction of a wrong charge and CGTMSE’s own fee rules are different matters. A loan account showing a guarantee fee does not, by itself, establish a right to reimbursement.
eligibility: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.
benefits:
The notification provided reimbursement of 100% of the guarantee-cover fee charged for qualifying collateral-free term loans or working-capital facilities under CGTMSE, for five years. The borrowing unit had to meet the scheme’s micro-enterprise conditions, be in commercial production and remain in regular production when assistance was disbursed. It also required Udyam registration, Haryana Udhyam Memorandum and applicable land-use or other approvals.

The benefit was tied to a specific fee. It was not a refund of the loan principal, all interest paid or every bank charge. Processing fees, insurance premiums and other debits should be identified separately before the claim amount is prepared. The notified lender and credit-facility conditions also need to be checked against the actual sanction.
application_process:
Start with the sanction letter and a bank confirmation identifying the CGTMSE-covered facility. Reconcile the guarantee fee charged, the period it relates to and the amount actually paid with the account statement. A generic bank statement description may need clarification from the branch.

Keep the enterprise registrations, commercial-production evidence, earlier claim acknowledgements and any sanction or deficiency correspondence together. The 2021 notification contained a three-month claim deadline linked to commencement of operations or notification, whichever was later. An existing file needs its own deadline and subsequent orders checked; a newly dated invoice does not necessarily reopen an expired claim period.

The notified process routes the claim through the Haryana department’s portal and District MSME Centre examination. The bank supplies credit and fee evidence; the department decides the incentive claim.

name: Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund
description:
The Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) supports qualifying investment in dairy, meat, animal feed and other specified animal-husbandry infrastructure through a lending and interest-support framework. It is relevant to processing and value addition as well as the other activities expressly identified in the programme.

The Department’s Operational Guidelines 3.0 reflect AHIDF’s continuation with the Dairy Processing Infrastructure Development Fund incorporated into it. Older FAQs that exclude dairy cooperatives do not describe the full revised applicant scope.
eligibility:
The revised framework states an approval-period endpoint of 31 March 2026. Clause 12.1 allows lenders to disburse for sanctioned projects approved on or before that date, but not beyond 31 March 2027. That later date is a disbursement provision for qualifying approved projects, not evidence of a fresh application window.

The longer programme sunset and repayment periods also serve different purposes. A new applicant needs any subsequent approval authority established before treating AHIDF as available for the proposal. An already approved borrower should check the remaining disbursement conditions and deadline with the lender.
benefits:
The guideline permits loans up to 90% of eligible project cost, based on a viable project and the lender’s assessment. Beneficiary contribution varies by enterprise category and financing requirements. The maximum loan share is not a promise that every applicant can contribute only 10%.

Interest assistance follows the applicable programme and sanction terms. The revised document preserves distinctions between earlier AHIDF and DIDF projects, so their historical rates should not be applied indiscriminately to another borrower.

The guideline excludes interest support on borrowing for specified costs, including land, working capital, pre-operative expenditure, existing infrastructure acquisition, old machinery and personal-use vehicles. It also links support to loan performance. Prepare the eligible borrowing schedule separately from the total project and monitor how support is credited to the loan account.
application_process:
The project report should connect raw-material supply, process capacity, product demand, machinery, utilities and financial projections. Assemble applicant and ownership records, land arrangements, technical quotations, permissions, the loan appraisal and financing commitments.

For an approved project, retain the original sanction, programme approval, disbursements, actual expenditure, completion and repayment records. A request to the lender should identify whether the issue concerns disbursement, interest-support credit or a project change. These are different stages with different evidence.

Read the AHIDF Operational Guidelines 3.0 and the Department’s programme overview. For a separate processing grant, assess CEFPPC on its own rules and non-duplication conditions.

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
description:
The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund helps finance eligible agricultural infrastructure through interest support on loans. It can be relevant to a warehouse, cold store, sorting and grading facility or qualifying processing project where the activity fits the scheme’s defined agricultural value chain.

AIF is a financing facility. Its value to a project lies in reducing the interest burden on qualifying borrowing and supporting access to credit guarantees. It does not turn the full cost of a facility into a capital grant, and the lender still assesses whether the business can repay the loan.
eligibility:
The September 2024 revised guidelines provide 3% annual interest subvention on eligible borrowing up to ₹2 crore, for a maximum of seven years. A larger loan can be considered, but that guideline limits the interest-supported portion to ₹2 crore. Credit-guarantee support is subject to the eligible borrower and guarantee framework.

The document gives the scheme an overall period through 2032–33, while setting the loan-disbursement period through 2025–26. These dates serve different purposes. The longer support period does not establish that new loan applications remain open after March 2026. A new proposal needs the latest disbursement authority and lender instructions checked before AIF is included in its financing plan.
benefits:
The revised list includes warehouses and silos, cold stores and cold-chain facilities, assaying, packaging, sorting, grading and specified logistics infrastructure. It also covers defined farming assets and certain farm-residue or waste-management activities. Each description has its own conditions; an agricultural connection in the business name is insufficient.

The 2024 revision distinguishes eligible primary processing and integrated primary-plus-secondary processing from standalone secondary processing, which is excluded. For example, a proposal must explain how the actual processing stages fit the crop-wise activity table. It is not enough to describe the entire investment simply as “food processing”.

Applicant categories include farmers, agri-entrepreneurs, start-ups, farmer producer organisations and other bodies identified in the guidelines. Some activities carry applicant-specific restrictions. Establish the applicant, asset, location and operating model together.
application_process:
A useful project file links the proposed asset to the produce it will handle, the capacity required and the income expected. For a warehouse, that means examining throughput, occupancy, storage charges and operating costs. For a processing line, it means showing the input, process stages, output and market.

Keep land or lease records, technical quotations, a cost breakdown, project report and proposed means of finance ready. Separate land, civil works, equipment and working capital. The bank needs repayment evidence and the scheme assessment needs eligible-activity evidence; the two reviews answer related but different questions.

Confirm the operative application route, submit the proposal and lender documentation, respond to appraisal queries, and preserve sanction and disbursement records. Interest support must be reconciled with the actual loan account over time.

name: Interest Subsidy for Textile Units
description:
Haryana’s textile Interest Subsidy Scheme addresses the cost of qualifying term loans for new projects, expansion, diversification and modernisation. It is relevant to the financing of the investment, so the bank sanction and interest actually paid are central to the assessment.

The scheme was notified on 5 July 2023 under the Haryana AatmaNirbhar Textile Policy. The May 2025 amendment extended the policy and its related schemes to 18 December 2026. That extension does not establish an applicant’s remaining support period or confirm that a particular claim can still be filed.
eligibility:
The notification sets separate arrangements for textile MSMEs and textile-machinery manufacturing MSMEs. For textile MSMEs, it specifies 6% interest support with a ₹20 lakh annual ceiling in B blocks, and 7% with respective annual ceilings of ₹30 lakh and ₹50 lakh in C and D blocks, for seven years. The machinery-manufacturing category has different limits.

A loan for unrelated expenditure should not be added to the claim merely because the borrower is a textile company. The project needs to satisfy the scheme’s new-investment or expansion definition and its eligible term-loan and production conditions.
benefits:
Prepare the bank sanction, drawdown schedule, interest certificate, repayment statement and the machinery or project schedule financed by the loan. Existing businesses should establish the fixed-investment baseline against which the expansion is being assessed. Identify sanction, disbursement, completion and commercial-production dates separately.

The scheme’s definition of expansion refers to more than 25% additional investment against existing gross fixed capital and completion within the stipulated period. This needs a defensible accounting and project record rather than a new label for ordinary expenditure.

For annual claims, reconcile the lender’s interest certificate with the books and loan statement. Separate penal interest, arrears or unrelated charges for review instead of applying the rate to all bank debits.

Can I receive both textile capital and interest assistance?

The provisions for each benefit and their interaction must be assessed against the same cost and financing schedule. Read Textile Capital Investment Subsidy as a separate component, not an automatic additional receipt.

description:

name: Capital Investment Subsidy for Textile Units
description:
Haryana’s Capital Investment Subsidy for Textile Units supports qualifying investment across the textile value chain. The applicable benefit depends on what the unit manufactures, its block location and whether the investment is a new project, expansion, diversification or modernisation.

The scheme notified on 5 July 2023 under the Haryana AatmaNirbhar Textile Policy has a later amendment that matters to investment planning. The 2 May 2025 notification extends the policy and its schemes to 18 December 2026. It also removes the capital-subsidy limit on the number of cases, subject to the overall approved budget. An operative policy period is not confirmation that budget remains available for a particular application.
eligibility:
The notification defines the cost base rather than using the project’s total headline value. Relevant investment may include specified plant and machinery, factory buildings, laboratories and utilities. It excludes items such as land, land development, working capital and listed preliminary or general civil expenditure.

For an expansion, the scheme definition refers to investment exceeding 25% of the existing gross fixed capital investment and completion within the stated period. Establish the existing investment baseline and the new project scope before preparing the calculation. Routine replacement purchases should not be labelled as a qualifying expansion without that assessment.
benefits:
The 2023 scheme separates general textile units, technical textiles and specified import-substitution or backward-integration projects, open-end spinning and waste-to-fibre units, and textile machinery manufacturers. Anchor units have a further category with different conditions. A project should be classified on its product, process and qualifying investment before choosing an assistance rate.

For general textile enterprises, the notified capital support is 30% of eligible investment, capped at ₹2.5 crore in B blocks, and 35%, capped at ₹3.5 crore in C and D blocks. Other categories have different limits. These figures describe that category under the cited scheme; they are not a single rate for every textile project.

The notification also contains category-specific enhancements and eligibility rules. Claiming a higher category needs evidence of the actual activity or qualifying ownership, not merely wording added to the project report.
application_process:
Prepare a process description, itemised fixed-capital schedule, quotations and invoices, proof of payment, ownership and site records, commercial-production dates and the existing investment baseline where relevant. Match the project category to the technical evidence. For waste-to-fibre or technical textiles, explain what the finished material is and how it is produced.

The complete source pack should include the 2023 scheme, the 2025 amendments and the relevant implementation memorandum. Check the applicable application trigger, current portal process, budget position and restrictions on claiming other assistance on the same expenditure. Preserve inspection, sanction and disbursement records separately.

Is Haryana textile support the same as ATUFS?

No. ATUFS is a separate central programme with its own historic implementation period and claim records. A Haryana application cannot be assessed by copying an ATUFS rate.

Does the extension guarantee acceptance until December 2026?

No. It extends the operative period. Eligibility, application timing, budget and approval still need to be established for the project.

name: Haryana Textile Park Scheme
description:
Haryana’s Textile Park Scheme supports the development of a location where multiple textile manufacturers can operate with planned infrastructure. The applicant’s role is the park promoter or developer. An individual textile factory has a different subsidy assessment, even when it will occupy land in the park.

The July 2023 scheme sits under the Haryana AatmaNirbhar Textile Policy. A May 2025 notification extended that policy and its schemes to 18 December 2026. This policy period does not, by itself, confirm approval capacity or an open submission facility for every park proposal.
eligibility:
The notified model requires at least 20 acres in a B, C or D category block, at least 10 manufacturing units and the prescribed aggregate fixed-capital investment of ₹30 crore. Location, the participant mix and the nature of manufacturing therefore matter before detailed infrastructure costs are prepared.

The developer should establish a coherent layout: industrial plots or premises, access, power, water, drainage and treatment facilities must serve the proposed occupiers. Land ownership and permissions need to support the intended development and use.
benefits:
The scheme provides specified relief on stamp duty and internal development charges, together with support for a qualifying common zero-liquid-discharge facility. The July 2023 notification sets out 50% assistance for the common ZLD facility, capped at ₹10 crore. Its technical scope, common use and approved expenditure must be established. The developer should keep this cost schedule separate from infrastructure sold or leased with individual plots.

name: Haryana Textile Cluster Development Scheme
description:
Textile businesses can share equipment and services that would be difficult for each unit to finance and operate alone. Haryana’s Textile Cluster Development Scheme provides a route for a qualifying group of textile MSMEs to establish a common facility centre.

The scheme is collective: the member units use the facility, while a dedicated organisation develops and operates it. Buying a machine for one member’s factory does not become a cluster project simply because other businesses support the application.
eligibility:
The July 2023 notification requires a group of at least 15 textile MSMEs within the prescribed 50-kilometre area, which may extend across Haryana districts. The special purpose vehicle, or SPV, must be constituted as a Section 8 not-for-profit company under the scheme.

This legal form matters. Member contributions, ownership of assets, access to facilities and continuing management should sit within that entity’s approved arrangements. name: Seed and Conversion Fund for EV Manufacturing
description:
The Seed and Conversion Fund in Haryana’s EV policy supports the complete conversion of an existing unit into EV, EV-component or EV-battery manufacturing. Despite the word “seed”, this provision is not a general early-stage start-up fund.

eligibility:

The conversion fund is framed for existing units converting completely. A new factory needs assessment under the appropriate EV capital-assistance provision.
